title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is the process used by plants, algae and some bacteria to convert light energy into chemical energy. During photosynthesis, plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil. Using energy from sunlight, they produce glucose and release oxygen as a by-product. This process takes place mainly in the chloroplasts of leaf cells, which contain a green pigment called chlorophyll.

title: Binary search
text: Binary search is a search algorithm that finds the position of a target value within a sorted array. It compares the target value to the middle element of the array. If they are not equal, the half in which the target cannot lie is eliminated and the search continues on the remaining half. Because the search space is halved at every step, the running time is logarithmic.

title: Solar System
text: The Solar System is made up of the Sun and the objects that orbit it, including eight planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets. The four inner planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, which are made mostly of rock and metal. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, while Uranus and Neptune are ice giants. The Sun contains more than ninety nine percent of the total mass of the system.

title: Hash table
text: A hash table is a data structure that maps keys to values. It uses a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets, from which the desired value can be found. Ideally the hash function assigns each key to a unique bucket, but most designs allow collisions where two keys produce the same index. One common way to handle collisions is separate chaining, in which each bucket holds a linked list.

title: Monsoon
text: A monsoon is a seasonal reversal of the prevailing wind direction that usually brings heavy rainfall to a region. In India the southwest monsoon arrives in June and retreats by September, and agriculture across the country depends heavily on it. The monsoon is caused by the different heating rates of land and sea during the year.

title: Water cycle
text: The water cycle describes the continuous movement of water on, above and below the surface of the Earth. Water evaporates from oceans and lakes, rises into the atmosphere, cools and condenses into clouds, and then falls back as rain or snow. Some of this water flows into rivers and returns to the sea, while some soaks into the ground.
